title: Measure information per search directly
why: Nothing measures how much a search teaches. KL(search policy || prior) and value change per search would give a real signal-per-compute number.
test: Log both per position in a short run, and check they separate full searches from cheap ones.

title: Connect updates 33 and 36 to the rating graph
why: Both swept the baseline 48-0, so they're only lower bounds. Whether the loop kept improving after them is unknown.
test: Play both against update 45 and update 42. About 40 games each is enough for a large gap.

title: Train the ownership head
why: Weight 0 in the bulk loop since 219d67a, with no recorded arena result. sigmago measured +194 ± 28 with ownership and score heads together, but -96 ± 49 on a smaller run.
test: Train on one frozen corpus at weights 0, 0.5 and 1.5, then arena at equal sims on both boards.

title: Retest a larger training window
why: 750k beat 250k 51-29 on the small board, while the big board was inconclusive. The loop runs 200k. This is the most direct evidence on getting more from existing data.
test: Replicate with a second seed at 500k and 750k, and weigh strength against training time.

title: Confirm 128 input as the efficient default
why: 128 searches 2-3.6x faster and scored 30-18 at equal time on the big board. One card plays 18.6k positions/s at 128, 7.4k at 192 and 4.1k at 256, so at 61 Elo a doubling 192 has to beat 128 by about 80 Elo at equal simulations and 256 by about 130.
test: Bootstrap at 128. Train a 192 net from scratch on the same window, then play them at equal time with --opponent-resolution on both boards. Move up once it wins.

title: Add a score head
why: Final scores have been recorded since 2026-09-24. Margin is richer than win or loss for each game.
test: Add after the ownership test, so the two effects can be told apart.

title: Branch from contested positions
why: sigmago's branch mining was never a fair test: 94% of roots were already decided, because it selected late positions.
test: Offline first: run several continuations from positions with values near even. Stop if they rarely disagree.

title: Revisit randomized search budgets
why: Gave 2.8x the games per hour, but 32 games were discarded and the pilot recipe was rejected. That doesn't rule out the idea.
test: Retry with a recipe that keeps a healthy policy target, judged at equal elapsed compute.

title: Add short-horizon value and opponent-move heads
why: Both can be labelled from existing games, adding more per-position signal.
test: Add one at a time, after ownership.

title: Rate models by game stage and board size
why: One rating hides regressions in the opening or endgame.
test: Extend arena records, and fit a rating per bucket.

title: Ablate the settled input plane
why: It's 92-96% of raster cost, and its strength benefit has never been measured.
test: Train with and without it on one corpus, then arena at equal time.

title: Settle one norm per block
why: Measured about 4-9% faster search, with mixed, inconclusive arenas.
test: Only worth a larger arena if 128 input is adopted first.

title: Tree reuse in self-play
why: Arena prototype scored 24-24 and 23-25, and inherited only 9-12 visits per hit.
test: No next step unless search budgets rise a lot.

title: Measure self-play on rented hardware
why: The engine work may have moved the limit from CPU to GPU.
test: Record generation throughput and GPU use on the rented box.

title: Rule regression fixtures
why: Capture cases have no reproducible shared positions.
test: Fixtures for nonlocal capture through pocket closure, disconnected self-capture, opponent removal reviving a group, and simultaneous captures run from one command and are shared with Rust.

title: Browser tests in check.sh
why: A stale UI test went unnoticed because nothing runs these automatically.
test: js-app/tests run headless on Linux. Today they need PowerShell and Windows Chrome.

title: Game-grouped validation
why: Adjacent positions from one game can land on both sides of the split, which makes validation loss optimistic.
test: All positions from one game land in one split, deterministically, tested with overlapping game IDs across shards.

title: Deterministic parallel arena
why: fp16 inference can reorder near-ties as batch shapes change.
test: Decide between bitwise repeatability and bounded stability, then show identical results across repeated fixed-seed runs.

title: Official vertex reach test
why: A bug in this check passes every test. A search of up to 3,000 random games found no position where it alone decides a group.
test: Find such a position, or prove the other two checks cover it.

title: Repetition and ko policy
why: Automated play reaches cycles, but it's unknown whether a strategically meaningful human cycle exists. Rule variants are in docs/history/GAMEPLAY_VARIANTS.md.
test: Find a position players would rationally repeat, then choose between unrestricted repetition, simple ko and superko.

title: Vgo learnings
why: Most runs in artifacts/old/ are in no note. Required before that folder is deleted.
test: Write one line per run in docs/FINDINGS.md: question, result, verdict, trust.

title: Decide the NumPy rasterizer
why: A hand-kept second rasterizer is a correctness risk if Rust covers every case.
test: Delete it unless something still needs the fallback.
